half_alu_fma12.srcC.label: hardware-run
half_alu_fma12.srcC.evidence: EXP-0203 (raw/g17p_run21,22,23,31,32 and raw/g17p_q41..q44, field `ext` byte_index 5); coverage re-derived by EXP-0214 (analysis/e0203_half.json)
half_alu_fma12.srcC.range: bits 40..47 (byte+5) dense 0..255, on 3 arms x 9 runs = 24 arm-run cells = 6144 cases; 256 distinct requested values and 256 distinct ACTUAL byte+5 encodings in every cell. Host oracle predicts the ENTIRE 16-word post-dump from the case's own pre-dump: 6144/6144 full-vector matches, 29 distinct predicted vectors and 29 distinct observed vectors per cell, 0 cross-run disagreements over 768 (arm,value) pairs. SCOPE BOUND: the semantic map is `bit0 = half, bits 1..6 = GPR index, bit 7 = don't-care`; only 64 of the 256 descriptors (GPR 0..15 and their bit-7 mirrors) name a register this carrier's 16-GPR window can see, and the remaining 192 are predicted AND observed to contribute 0 -- a carrier property checked per run by the __ctl_unseeded control, NOT a hardware statement about GPRs 16..63. An emitter may use srcC to name r0..r15; r16..r63 are unvalidated.
half_alu_fma12.srcC.note: Gates re-derived from raw by EXP-0214. Gate A: 49,152/49,152 ext byte-sweep cases have requested value == the value decoded from the actual dispatched bytes, 0 mismatches. G1 span-only: 6144/6144 differ from the arm anchor ONLY inside byte+5. G2: 6144/6144 status OK + seed_ok + sentinels + not victim. G3: 0/768 cross-run disagreements. G4 moved: 6096/6144 (the 48 non-movers are the anchor's own byte+5 value and its bit-7 mirror, one pair per cell). G5: 6144/6144 oracle_match with 29 distinct predicted post-digests (a constant oracle was a pre-registered FAILURE). G6 falsifiers all fired: __fals_F1_null 90/90 non-match with null_match true, __fals_F2_opsel 60/60 non-match, __fals_F4_dstshift 90/90 non-match. G7: 6144/6144 hw_markers == the anchor's 4. Gate B detection power in this exact dimension: __ctl_live_srcA 480/480 oracle_match across 8 distinct seeded source descriptors. Gate B section 6 (two disjoint readback plans): MET -- arms F12_EXT_A/B run layout HI, F12_EXT_C runs layout LO with the destination moved r1 -> r7 (Amendment 03). Bit 7 measured a don't-care, not assumed: descriptors d and d|0x80 produced byte-identical 16-word post-dumps on 128/128 pairs. Gate E: INHERITED, not direct -- EXP-0210 confirmed EXP-0203's q43/q44 quiet pair at 100.0000% for `dst`/`dstlo`/`b3`; the byte+5 cases are records in those same two captures, so the quiet window is the same window, but EXP-0210 did not name this field. CAVEAT ON THE FROZEN GATE: EXP-0203's PRE_REGISTRATION bound `ext` (then 64 bits, 2048 of 2^64 sampled) to `untested` whatever happened. That bound was about the 64-bit parent's coverage; `srcC` is an 8-bit field EXP-0212 created and it IS densely covered. H2 pre-registered `byte+5 is the third fp16 operand's half-register descriptor` with an explicit refuter (`a byte+5 value whose observed result is not the frozen oracle's prediction`), and the refuter did not fire once in 6144 cases. The G1..G7 criteria were frozen; the field they are applied to was not.

half_alu_fma12.lensel.label: untested
half_alu_fma12.lensel.evidence: EXP-0203 (raw g17p_run21..32, g17p_q41..q44, field `ext` byte_index 4); re-derived in EXP-0214 analysis/e0203_half.json
half_alu_fma12.lensel.range: bits 32..33 (byte+4 & 3), all 4 values dispatched, 1664 cases each (the byte+4 sweep is a full 4 x 64 factorial of lensel x mods), 3 arms x 9 runs. LIVE on a silicon-side observable: the surviving-length-marker count partitions EXACTLY by bit 32 -- lensel 0 -> 2 markers (1664/1664), 1 -> 4 (1664/1664), 2 -> 2 (1662/1664, 2 unmeasured), 3 -> 4 (1663/1664, 1 unmeasured). Bit 33 is inert on that observable. NOT PROMOTED: no frozen model maps the 4 values to 4 lengths, and the hardware's 2-way split CONTRADICTS the db length map.
half_alu_fma12.lensel.note: Six axes: geometry `geometry-mapped` (4/4 values reached the dispatched bytes; Gate A 49,152/49,152 on the parent byte sweeps); liveness `live` (the marker count is a hardware measurement of consumed length, not our tokenizer's opinion -- EXP-0203 Amendment 03b makes exactly that distinction; the partition is identical in 23 of 24 arm-run cells and the 24th differs only by 3 unmeasured cases); semantics `hypothesis` (H2 named byte+4 bits 0..1 `the length selector` but registered no per-value length model and no refuter for it; the byte+4 sweep was pre-registered as a declared HAZARD, not as this field's evidence); recipe `not-generated`; target `G17P-direct`; reproducibility `auditable`, Gate E inherited from EXP-0203's q43/q44 pair rather than named by EXP-0210. FINDING FOR A SUCCESSOR, not a promotion: db.json's length map makes the 12-byte form reachable only at lensel == 3 and reads lensel == 1 as an 8-byte `half_alu_ext8`, but the silicon's marker count is IDENTICAL at 1 and 3 and differs at 0 and 2. Either the length map's 1 vs 3 distinction is wrong, or the marker observable cannot resolve 8 vs 12 bytes in this splice layout. One dense byte+4 sweep with a marker plan that can count 8 vs 12 separately settles it. Until then the honest reading is `live on a 2-valued length observable; the 4-value length map is unconfirmed`.

half_alu_fma12.mods.label: untested
half_alu_fma12.mods.evidence: EXP-0203 (field `ext` byte_index 4, restricted to lensel == 3); re-derived in EXP-0214 analysis/e0203_half.json
half_alu_fma12.mods.range: bits 34..39 (byte+4 bits 2..7), all 64 values dispatched at lensel == 3 (the 12-byte form), 24 cases each = 1536 cases over 3 arms x 9 runs; hardware identity preserved 1535/1536. LIVE: only 6 of 64 values (2,3,4,5,6,7) ever reproduce the anchor's arithmetic, and only 2 of those (4,5 -- 4 is the compiler's own) do so in all 24 cells; values 2,3 match in 9/24 cells and 6,7 in 15/24, i.e. the effect is CARRIER-DEPENDENT. NOT PROMOTED: no frozen model is indexed by this field.
half_alu_fma12.mods.note: Six axes: geometry `geometry-mapped`; liveness `live`; semantics `unknown` -- there is no pre-registered predictor for `mods`. H2 called byte+4 bits 2..7 `operation modifiers` and stopped there. The structure visible in the raw is real and worth a successor's pre-registration, but it is POST-HOC and must not be labelled: values 8..31 and 40..63 all fit the frozen alternate model `abs(a)*b` (the addend is dropped), 18/24 cells each; values 32..39 produce the correct arithmetic RESULT (oracle_result_match up to 24/24) while FAILING the full-vector match (0/24), which is the signature of a correct result plus an extra side effect -- consistent with the source-release behaviour EXP-0203's PRE_REGISTRATION section 4.1 measured at byte+4 = 0x93 -- and values 0..7 spread over `abs(a)*b+c`, `a*b+c` and `abs(a)*b-c`. Reading those fits as a modifier map would be exactly the EXP-0169 error the corrections name: the 9 models were frozen for a different question and their fit pattern is a hint, not an oracle. recipe `not-generated`; target `G17P-direct`; reproducibility `auditable`, Gate E inherited.

half_pack.dst.label: untested
half_pack.dst.evidence: EXP-0203 (all 15,872 half_pack records across raw/pilot01 and 9 gated runs); census in EXP-0214 analysis/e0203_half.json
half_pack.dst.range: bits 4..7 (byte0 high nibble). NOT SWEPT AT ALL: zero records in the whole experiment carry `field == "dst"` for half_pack. Exactly 2 of 16 nibbles ever reached the hardware inside an actual half_pack instruction -- nibble 1 (9,532 records, arms HP_A/HP_B, layout HI) and nibble 7 (6,300 records, arms HP_C/HP_D, layout LO). Both are FIXED ARM CONSTANTS -- the layout's destination register -- not swept values. A third nibble, 14, appears in 20 records but those are `ec00ec00`, the __fals_F1_null falsifier's mov_imm pads, i.e. not this instruction at all. 14 of 16 values untested.
half_pack.dst.note: Six axes: geometry `unverified` for 14 of 16 values (the 2 that ran are ledger-verified); liveness `carrier-undecidable` -- with only two values, both constants, there is no sweep in which the field could have been seen to move, and the one falsifier that touches the destination (__fals_F4_dstshift) does not change the BYTES at all: it dispatches the anchor unmodified and asks the ORACLE to predict a shifted destination, so it is a check on the oracle's discrimination, not a probe of this field; semantics `unknown`; recipe `not-generated`; target `G17P-direct`; reproducibility `auditable`. This is the field EXP-0212's own RESULTS section 8 flagged as its one residual risk, and the risk is real: `range` is free prose, so no tool can read `2 of 16` out of it, and the sibling field `half_alu_fma12.dst` -- same 4-bit position, same family -- IS densely swept (16/16 in 4 arms), which makes it easy to assume by symmetry that this one is too. It is not. Promoting it would be the exact failure the corrections call promoting on a carrier that could not see the effect.

irotate.rot_dst.label: untested
irotate.rot_dst.evidence: EXP-0202 (arms ROT/rot_alu#0/operands_b3 and ROT/rot_k5#0/operands_b3 in raw/g17p_quiet03, quiet04, g17p_20260830_run03, run04); Gate A and coverage re-derived in EXP-0214 analysis/e0202_irotate.json
irotate.rot_dst.range: bits 24..31 (byte+3), dense 0..255 on 2 carriers x 4 runs = 2048 cases, 256 distinct actual encodings per arm. Reproducible: 0/512 cross-run outcome disagreements. Outcome map: 2 of 256 values (0,1) reproduce the carrier vector; 64 of 256 (192..255, contiguous) FAULT; the rest split by carrier -- 752 wrong_value on rot_alu and 752 silent_zero on rot_k5, i.e. even the failure class depends on the carrier. NOT PROMOTED: the pre-registered predictor was refuted on 520 of 2048 cases.
irotate.rot_dst.note: Six axes: geometry `geometry-mapped` -- Gate A re-derived 2048/2048 (requested_bytes == actual_bytes AND the (24,8) span of the actual bytes decodes to the requested value), 0 encoding collisions. The driver's own `ledger_ok` reads False on all 2048 because it compares against the tokenizer's decode of the WHOLE 40-bit parent `operands`; EXP-0202's analysis/verdicts.py::ledger already documents and corrects that, and after EXP-0212's split the sub-span IS the db field, so the correct assertion passes. liveness `live` but role unknown; semantics `unknown` -- the arm's oracle rule is `exact_iff_compiled`, which predicts the carrier vector at the compiler's own value and a bare `broken` everywhere else. That is a liveness hypothesis written as an oracle, not a map from value to effect, and it cannot distinguish wrong_value from silent_zero from fault. It was REFUTED on 520 cases. EXP-0202's own RESULTS says it plainly: `every arm's pre-registered predictor was refuted somewhere except the four operands_b6 arms`, and it treats the same situation on iunary.b1/opsel as `live but role unknown -- no promotion`. The name `dst` comes from a census byte-diff over compiled amounts and EXP-0139's reading of the same blob in iunary/ibitcount -- corpus correlation, and no experiment has ever read back a rotate result from a register this field selected. recipe `not-generated`; target `G17P-direct`; reproducibility `auditable`, Gate E inherited from EXP-0210's confirmation of EXP-0202's `irotate.operands` (the quiet03/quiet04 pair), which is literally these records. The contiguous 192..255 fault region is a genuine new hardware fact worth documenting on its own -- reproduced in 4 runs on 2 carriers with 0 disagreements -- but a fault map is not a semantic map.

irotate.op_enable.label: untested
irotate.op_enable.evidence: EXP-0202 (arms ROT/rot_alu#0/operands_b4 and ROT/rot_k5#0/operands_b4, same four runs); re-derived in EXP-0214 analysis/e0202_irotate.json
irotate.op_enable.range: bits 32..39 (byte+4), dense 0..255 on 2 carriers x 4 runs = 2048 cases, 256 distinct actual encodings per arm (the two arms dispatch the SAME 256 byte strings in two different programs, so 256 distinct encodings in total -- reported per arm because that is the meaningful denominator). 0/512 cross-run disagreements, 0 faults. 128 of 256 values reproduce the carrier vector -- exactly the values with bit 1 set. NOT PROMOTED: the pre-registered predictor was refuted on 1016 of 2048 cases.
irotate.op_enable.note: Six axes: geometry `geometry-mapped`, Gate A re-derived 2048/2048; liveness `live` -- the 128/128 split by bit 33 is sharp and perfectly reproducible; semantics `unknown`. This is the most refuted arm in the set: `exact_iff_compiled` predicted that only the compiler's own value would reproduce, and 127 other values did, on both carriers in all four runs. A refuted model is a result, not a licence -- what the data supports is `bit 33 gates whether the operation happens`, which is a POST-HOC hypothesis with no independent predictor and no test of the other 7 bits' role. The `op-enable gate` name is EXP-0202's own post-hoc reading of the same numbers, and its Limitations section explicitly classes such refinements as `pre-registerable hypotheses for a successor, not as mapped semantics`. recipe `not-generated`; target `G17P-direct`; reproducibility `auditable`, Gate E inherited via EXP-0210's confirmation of `irotate.operands`.

simd_reduce.op_hi.label: untested
simd_reduce.op_hi.evidence: EXP-0205 (field `op`, byte+1 dense 0..255, arms sr_sum/sr_max/sr_scan/sr_fsum in raw/g17p_quiet01..04 and g17p_20260830_runB01/B02); re-derived in EXP-0214 analysis/e0205_op_hi.json
simd_reduce.op_hi.range: bits 11..15 (byte+1 bits 3..7), all 32 values dispatched as the high 5 bits of a dense 0..255 byte+1 sweep, 8 times each per arm-run cell, over 4 reduce carriers x 6 gated runs = 24 cells = 6144 cases; 256 distinct actual byte+1 encodings per cell. Gate A 6144/6144 (requested bytes == actual bytes AND requested == decoded, from the raw's own ledger block). ACCEPTED-INERT in this envelope: the hardware observable is a function of bits [2:0] alone -- period 8 holds in 24 of 24 cells -- and 0 of 1024 (arm,value) pairs disagree across runs. NOT PROMOTED: an inertness reading is not a label.
simd_reduce.op_hi.note: Six axes: geometry `geometry-mapped`; liveness `accepted-inert`; semantics `unknown`; recipe `not-generated`; target `G17P-direct`; reproducibility `independently-confirmed` for the OBSERVATION (Gate E inherited -- EXP-0210 confirmed EXP-0205's `simd_reduce.op` on the quiet pair and these are the same records). SAFE NEGATIVE WORDING per corrections section 7: `inert in 0..31 dense x 4 reduce carriers x 6 gated runs on G17P at fixed op[2:0]; global role unknown`. Section 7's bar is NOT met and this is why it stays untested: (a) 4 carriers, but sr_sum / sr_max / sr_scan / sr_fsum share one stage, one readback plan and one 32-lane u32 observation path, so by section 7's own rule (`two generated carriers with the same leaf callee, state shape, or observation path count as one method`) that is one carrier class, not three; (b) the positive control is good but partial -- the low 3 bits of the SAME byte produce 4 to 6 distinct hardware observables per carrier, so the readback demonstrably sees byte+1 change, yet nothing tests the dimension a high-order opcode-extension bit would plausibly control; (c) no interaction tests against `dtype`, `shape`, `opcls`, `scope` or `cache`, and EXP-0212 refused to narrow `simd_reduce.dtype` for exactly this reason -- its bit 4 is `f16_incl_scan` and no carrier is fp16, so the same blind dimension may hide op_hi's role too; (d) no independent method. MEASUREMENT NOTE worth carrying forward: this test is only valid on the hardware observable. Including `observed.gputime_ns` makes period-8 fail in 24/24 cells (nondeterministic timing -- the same defect EXP-0202 found in tools/agx-isa/wave_audit.py), and including the derived `outcome` label also makes it fail, because `outcome` is scored against a per-VALUE oracle and therefore varies with op_hi even where the silicon does not. Both false negatives were reproduced during this analysis before being excluded.

frag_depth_store.b1_lo.label: untested
frag_depth_store.b1_lo.evidence: EXP-0199 (field `byte1`, dense 0..255, carriers c_depth and c_depth2 in raw/g17p_conf01, conf04, quietconf01, quietconf02, plus the pre-conf run01a/run02a pair); re-derived in EXP-0214 analysis/e0199_frag_depth_store.json
frag_depth_store.b1_lo.range: bit 8 (byte+1 bit 0), both values dispatched INSIDE the accepted region in every one of 10 arm-run cells. The descriptor's match pins only bits 9..10, and the measured accepted set is exactly (v & 0x06) == 0x04 -- 64 of 256 in 9 of the 10 cells, and 63 in the tenth (g17p_conf04/c_depth2, where the one missing value 236 is an InnocentVictim fault and is `ok` in the other three runs). Among those 64 accepted values there is exactly ONE distinct hardware signature per cell -- identical colour triple, depth triple, colour-surface hash and depth-surface hash -- so this bit is accepted-inert over its full 2-value domain. NOT PROMOTED: inertness is not a label.
frag_depth_store.b1_lo.note: Six axes: geometry `geometry-mapped` (Gate A: 4096/4096 conf-run cases have the actual dispatched byte equal to the requested value; the 1024 cases in the pre-conf run01a/run02a pair carry no ledger block at all and are reported separately, not counted); liveness `accepted-inert`; semantics `unknown`; recipe `not-generated`; target `G17P-direct`; reproducibility `auditable`, Gate E `MET, bounded` per EXP-0210 -- every residual cross-run flip is fault<->clean, and this analysis confirms it: every anomalous case in these arms is either kIOGPUCommandBufferCallbackErrorInnocentVictim (a measurement_failure by Gate E, never a hardware outcome) or a hang, and only one value (byte+1 = 177, which is in the REJECTED set anyway) repeats a genuine hang in 2 of 4 runs. Detection power is genuinely established on the same instruction and the SAME observable -- this experiment reads the Depth32Float attachment back per pixel for the first time, b5 bit 1 collapses depth to 0.0 on 128/256 values, and byte+1's own match bits discard the tile on 192/256 -- so this is a real accepted-inert reading, not a blind one. It still stays untested because section 7 wants three structurally different carrier classes and this has two (c_depth and c_depth2 differ in their depth and colour functions, which is a good adversarial pair for the INSTRUCTION's role but is one fragment stage, one attachment configuration and one observation path), no interaction tests against b3/b4/b5, and no independent method. SAFE WORDING: `inert in 0..1 x 2 fragment carriers with a depth attachment x 5 gated captures on G17P, within the accepted byte+1 region; global role unknown`.

frag_depth_store.b2.label: untested
frag_depth_store.b2.evidence: EXP-0199 (field `byte2`, dense 0..255, carriers c_depth and c_depth2, same five capture pairs); re-derived in EXP-0214 analysis/e0199_frag_depth_store.json
frag_depth_store.b2.range: bits 16..23 (byte+2), dense 0..255 on 2 carriers x 5 captures = 10 cells = 2560 cases. db.json declares this byte a full-byte match of 0x54 and the hardware does NOT enforce it: every value is accepted in 8 of the 10 cells, with exactly ONE distinct hardware signature (colour triple, depth triple, and both surface hashes) across all 256 values. NOT PROMOTED: accepted-inert over the tested envelope is not a label.
frag_depth_store.b2.note: Six axes: geometry `geometry-mapped` (Gate A 4096/4096 over the ledgered byte1+byte2 conf cases); liveness `accepted-inert`; semantics `unknown`; recipe `not-generated`; target `G17P-direct`; reproducibility `auditable`, Gate E `MET, bounded`. The two non-clean cells are both in g17p_conf04, and every one of their anomalies is classified rather than counted: 4 kIOGPUCommandBufferCallbackErrorInnocentVictim faults (measurement_failure under Gate E, and EXP-0210 measured EXP-0199's InnocentVictim count going 4 and 16 -> 0 and 0 on the quiet machine), 1 genuine hang at value 249 that does not repeat in the other 3 runs, and 1 `both_moved` at value 19 that likewise appears in 1 of 4 runs and is therefore an unrepeated single-run event, not a hardware fact -- Gate E requires such claims to be repeated in isolation. Detection power is proven on the same instruction and observable by b3, b4, b5 and byte+1, so unlike most inertness readings this one is not blind. It stays untested for the section 7 reasons: two carriers of one class, one observation path, no interaction tests, no independent method -- and because the interesting claim here is a NEGATIVE one about a byte the database calls a match, which corrections section 7 says needs the strongest evidence, not the weakest. The db-defect finding (`match [16,8,84]` is not enforced) is EXP-0199's and stands on its own; it is a statement about the descriptor, not a label for the field.

pop_reconverge.reserved_hi.label: untested
pop_reconverge.reserved_hi.evidence: EXP-0206 (field `reserved`, 52 sampled 16-bit values, carriers cf_ifnl / cf_nl2 / cl_atomic in raw/g17p_20260830_run03..07, g17p_quiet02, and EXP-0213's S1/S2 captures); re-derived in EXP-0214 analysis/e0206_reserved_hi.json
pop_reconverge.reserved_hi.range: bits 40..47 (byte+5). The parent sweep SAMPLED 52 of 65,536 16-bit values, which reach 25 distinct high bytes -- but only 9 of them ({0,1,2,4,8,16,32,64,128}) occur with a zero sibling low byte, and only those 9 are interpretable, because the LOW byte is load-bearing: on the cf_ifnl carrier all 43 nonzero-low-byte cases give wrong_value. Within those 9 clean points the result is ok 9/9 with exactly ONE hardware signature, on all 3 carriers and in all 12 arm-run cells. So: 9 of 256 values tested, 247 untested. NOT PROMOTED -- 9 of 256 is a sample, not a sweep.
pop_reconverge.reserved_hi.note: Six axes: geometry `geometry-mapped` for the 9 values that ran -- Gate A re-derived, 624/624 cases have the (40,8) span of the actual bytes equal to the requested value >> 8; liveness `accepted-inert in a 9-of-256 sample`, and that reading is worth very little here, which is the point: the sibling field `pop_reconverge.reserved` (32,8) reads INERT on cf_nl2 and cl_atomic (43/43 ok) and LIVE on cf_ifnl (43/43 wrong_value), and the three carriers differ essentially only in lane-dependent divergence. Two of the three carriers are therefore demonstrably blind in this dimension, so an inert reading of the high byte rests on one carrier with detection power and 9 sampled values, 8 of which are single-bit patterns. EXP-0206's own verdict table records the parent as `live (1 of 3) - carrier-undecidable (2 of 3)`, `hypothesis - all 3 models refuted`, `untested`, and its next-experiment recommendation 2 is to sweep this region densely on lane-dependent carriers. semantics `unknown`; recipe `not-generated`; target `G17P-direct`; reproducibility `auditable`. Gate E is PARTIAL and inherited: EXP-0210 re-derived that EXP-0206's run05/run07 pair (cf_ifnl -- the one live carrier) really was quiet, but its cf_nl2 / cl_atomic / cl_leaf / cl_chain arms were NOT REACHED because on a quiet machine those encodings hang. So the carrier that matters has a quiet pair and the two that read inert do not.
